theme.title: Around the League
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did Giannis's 2018–19 Milwaukee Bucks win?
questions.note: 60 wins, the best record in the NBA.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bucks finished the regular season with a 60–22 record

funFacts.text: Milwaukee moved from the Bradley Center to the new Fiserv Forum before the campaign.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Bucks moved from the Bradley Center to the new Fiserv Forum

funFacts.text: Mike Budenholzer arrived as the team's head coach in May of the preceding offseason.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: On May 17, 2018, the Bucks hired Mike Budenholzer as head coach

funFacts.text: The Bucks finished with the best team defensive rating in the league.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Bucks had the best team defensive rating in the NBA

questions.prompt: On January 7, 2003, Kobe Bryant set the NBA record for threes in a game. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He broke an NBA record for three-pointers on January 7, 2003, when he made 12 against the Seattle SuperSonics.

funFacts.text: The Lakers finished that season with a 50–32 record before losing to San Antonio in the playoffs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After finishing 50–32 in the regular season, the Lakers floundered in the playoffs

funFacts.text: Kobe was voted to both the All-NBA and All-Defensive First Teams that year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He was once again voted to both the All-NBA and All-Defensive First Teams

funFacts.text: Despite his scoring records, Bryant finished third in the league MVP voting that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: and came in third for the MVP award

questions.prompt: In the 1987 title clincher, the Lakers won the third quarter 30 to what?
questions.context: 1987 NBA Finals · Game 6 · at Los Angeles

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Lakers outscored the Celtics 30–12 in the third quarter for an 18-point turnaround

funFacts.text: Boston reached the Finals with its bench depleted by injuries to Bill Walton and Scott Wedman.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Their bench, an asset of the previous year's team, was decimated by injuries

funFacts.text: Magic Johnson had only four points at halftime before the Lakers seized control.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Magic Johnson had only four points at the half

funFacts.text: James Worthy dove for a loose ball, kept it inbounds and fed Magic for a momentum-changing dunk.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Worthy went to the floor, batted the ball inbounds to a breaking Magic Johnson

questions.prompt: About how many points per game did the 1966–67 Sixers average?
questions.note: About 125, with the league’s best shooting.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The team averaged a record 125 points per game, leading all teams in shooting accuracy

funFacts.text: Hal Greer led a balanced offense with Chet Walker and Billy Cunningham also scoring heavily.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Hal Greer with 22 points & Chet Walker & Billy Cunningham with 19 points each

funFacts.text: The Sixers' prolific scoring was paired with league-leading shooting accuracy, not just more attempts.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: leading all teams in shooting accuracy

funFacts.text: Chamberlain operated as an offensive distributor, establishing a new assists benchmark for centers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Wilt Chamberlain's 8 assists per game set a record for centers

questions.prompt: In Game 4 of the 2008 Finals, the Lakers set a Finals record for a first-quarter lead. How big was it?
questions.note: 21 points, 35–14. Boston came back to win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a 35–14 lead after the first quarter, which was the largest first-quarter lead in NBA Finals history

funFacts.text: Boston's reserve Eddie House finally put the Celtics ahead with a fourth-quarter jumper.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Celtics took their first lead in the game when Celtics' reserve Eddie House

funFacts.text: Boston's bench outscored Los Angeles's reserves as Eddie House and James Posey changed the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 29 of those points coming from House and James Posey

funFacts.text: Paul Pierce's unexpected 'Wheelchair Game' return was another defining moment of this series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
